note: Normal-operation patterns that are often reported as faults. Knowledge for the reasoner: each entry says what is normal, why, and the warning signs that would make it a fault. General appliance-operation knowledge, as stated in typical UK manufacturer manuals.

entries.normal: Eco 40-60 and cotton eco programmes routinely run 3-4 hours; they save energy by washing cooler for longer. The displayed time also adjusts during the cycle as the machine weighs the load and checks foam and balance.
entries.warning: The cycle never finishes, the display counts down then resets repeatedly, or a code appears.

entries.normal: Drums pause between tumbles, while soaking, while weighing the load and before spins. Pauses of a few minutes are normal.
entries.warning: It stops for more than 15-20 minutes, shows a code, or water is left in at the end.

entries.normal: A little water left in the folds of the door seal or the detergent drawer after a wash is normal.
entries.warning: Water above the bottom of the door glass, or clothes still soaking.

entries.normal: Machines deliberately skip or reduce the spin when a load is unbalanced (one heavy item, a small load, a duvet or a bath mat). Clothes then come out wet.
entries.warning: It never spins even with a normal mixed load, or it hums without draining.

entries.normal: Door-lock clicks and a short whirr as the drum turns to weigh the load at the start are normal.
entries.warning: Repeated clicking with the door never locking, or a grinding noise.

entries.normal: A small amount of clean water around the filter or sump (a cup or so, under the filter level) is normal: it keeps the seals wet.
entries.warning: Dirty water above the filter, water covering the base, or water that smells.

entries.normal: Plastics stay wet after a dishwasher cycle, especially on Eco programmes and in dishwashers without heated drying: plastic holds little heat. Opening the door slightly at the end helps.
entries.warning: Glass and china also come out cold and wet, or the dishes come out cold.

entries.normal: Dishwasher Eco programmes often take 3-4 hours. They clean at a lower temperature for longer.
entries.warning: The time on other programmes is also far longer than the manual says, or it never finishes.

entries.normal: A short pump hum or gurgle while draining is normal.
entries.warning: Grinding, a loud hum with no water leaving, or water remaining.

entries.normal: Fridges cycle on and off all day. A click as the compressor starts or stops, followed by a steady hum, is normal. Inverter compressors hum continuously at varying speeds.
entries.warning: Rapid repeated clicking every few minutes with the fridge getting warm, or a loud buzz with no cooling.

entries.normal: Gurgling, bubbling, hissing or trickling sounds are refrigerant moving around the circuit, and cracking or popping is plastic expanding during defrost. All normal.
entries.warning: Noise with the fridge getting warm, or a continuous loud hiss with an oily residue.

entries.normal: In most fridges the back wall frosts while the compressor runs and then melts and runs into the drain channel when it stops: a thin layer of frost or droplets that comes and goes is normal. Frost-free freezers defrost automatically every few hours and may hiss or drip during that time.
entries.warning: Thick ice that never clears, water pooling on the shelves or floor, or the fridge getting warm.

entries.normal: The sides or front between the doors of many fridge-freezers get warm: the condenser and anti-condensation pipes run there. Normal.
entries.warning: The outside is hot to touch with the inside not cooling, or a burning smell.

entries.normal: Fridges run longer after being loaded with warm food, in hot weather, after a power cut or after the door has been opened often. Modern inverter models run for long periods at low speed.
entries.warning: It runs constantly and is still not cold.

entries.normal: A new or moved fridge-freezer should stand upright for several hours before switching on (check the manual) and takes up to 24 hours to reach temperature.
entries.warning: Still not cold after 24 hours.

entries.normal: Induction hobs buzz, hum or whistle at high power, especially with heavy or multi-layer pans; they click as zones pulse at low settings; and a cooling fan runs during and after cooking.
entries.warning: Loud cracking, a burning smell, sparks, or the hob switching off with a code.

entries.normal: Induction zones only heat magnetic pans of the right size. A flashing pan symbol (often 'U' or a pan icon) means no suitable pan is detected. A magnet sticking firmly to the pan base shows it is induction-compatible.
entries.warning: A known induction-compatible pan of the right size is not detected on any zone.

entries.normal: An 'H' on a ceramic or induction zone after use is the residual-heat warning: the surface is still hot.
entries.warning: The H shows on a zone that has not been used.

entries.normal: Cooling fans keep running after an oven (or a combination microwave) is switched off until the inside has cooled, often 10-30 minutes.
entries.warning: The fan never stops even when the oven is cold.

entries.normal: Oven elements and the thermostat light switch on and off repeatedly once the set temperature is reached. That cycling is how the temperature is held.
entries.warning: The oven never reaches temperature, or the elements never come on.

entries.normal: A new oven gives off smoke and a smell the first few times as protective coatings burn off. Manuals recommend running it empty at a high temperature for about an hour with the window open.
entries.warning: The smell continues after several uses or smells of burning plastic or wiring.

entries.normal: Microwaves hum while heating, and the cooling fan may run for a while after the cycle.
entries.warning: Sparks, a burning smell, grinding or a loud buzz with no heating.

entries.normal: Steam and condensation on the door and some light visible around the door edge are normal.
entries.warning: Sparks, a damaged door or seal, or the microwave running with the door open.

entries.normal: Most dryers turn the drum occasionally after the end of the programme (anti-crease) until the door is opened.
entries.warning: It keeps heating after the end, or runs with the door open.

entries.normal: Sensor-dry programmes adjust the remaining time as they measure moisture; the time going up or down is normal.
entries.warning: Clothes always come out damp or the time never counts down.

entries.normal: Heat-pump dryers dry at a lower temperature and take noticeably longer than vented or condenser dryers; clothes come out warm rather than hot.
entries.warning: Clothes are still wet at the end of a full cycle with clean filters and an emptied water tank.

entries.normal: Vacuums have a thermal cut-out that switches them off when airflow is blocked or the filter is clogged; after cooling (often 30-60 minutes) they work again. This protects the motor and is not itself a fault.
entries.warning: It cuts out even with clean filters and no blockage, or there is a burning smell.

entries.normal: A cordless vacuum pulsing on and off is its warning that airflow is blocked or the filter needs washing (or the battery is not making contact); it is protection, not a fault in itself.
entries.warning: It still pulses with clear airways, a clean dry filter and a charged battery.
